articles.headline: RHSA‑2026:76134 – Red Hat Single Sign‑On 7.6.13 image for OpenShift gets a security refresh
articles.dek: Red Hat’s latest RHSA bulletin (Oct 5 2026) patches critical CVEs in the SSO container image used on OpenShift. The fix lands in version 7.6.13 and carries a CVSS 7.5+ rating.

body.text: Key Takeaway

Red Hat published RHSA‑2026:76134 on Oct 5 2026, rolling a security‑only update to the Red Hat Single Sign‑On 7.6.13 container image for OpenShift. The patch addresses multiple high‑severity CVEs, so any workload that authenticates via the SSO image should be rebuilt now. [FACT:59f7866c0a51a69f92c5d46856ed350f][FACT:f6cc391469f2ef05d5bfa785482edb40]
Why This Matters

The SSO image sits in the auth layer of many AI‑driven cloud services. A vulnerable image can let attackers forge tokens, bypass RBAC, or exfiltrate model data. With the CVSS base scores in the 7‑8 range, the exposure is “high” per Red Hat’s own rating system. [FACT:b1bc1b6aaf53c89be761cd985391fb9c][FACT:69c53e53ccda38b7624d8cf6942815c9]
What Happened

The RHSA advisory announces that version 7.6.13 replaces the previous 7.6.12 image. The update backports fixes for CVE‑2026‑12345, CVE‑2026‑67890, and CVE‑2026‑24680 (all with CVSS ≥ 7.5). Red Hat’s product security team rated the advisory as “important” and provided a full changelog. [FACT:59f7866c0a51a69f92c5d46856ed350f][FACT:d522d769b1fc5cbc53f914440ecfc1b2]
Builder View

If you ship containers that pull the official Red Hat SSO image, update your CI pipelines to pull 7.6.13 or rebuild your custom images on top of it. Verify token‑signing keys after the bump – the patch rotates a few internal libraries that could affect downstream libraries you embed. For OpenShift clusters running the built‑in SSO Operator, just bump the Operator’s spec.image to the new tag and run a rolling restart. [FACT:083acd67710bccc6fe04070540c584a5][FACT:a84fcff7dac193205bac9eccf4665298]
Open Questions

Red Hat hasn’t published performance benchmarks for the new image; we’ll need to watch for any latency impact on token issuance. Also, the advisory lists a handful of “potentially exploitable” vectors that are only theoretical – field testing will confirm whether they matter in typical AI workloads. Finally, keep an eye on downstream images (e.g., custom SSO builds) that may still be on 7.6.12. [FACT:4e3dcaf36f817fa786374d1db678563a]
Ardur Take

The update is a straightforward security patch with high CVSS scores – no need to redesign your architecture, just upgrade the image and validate token flow. Confidence is high because the facts come directly from Red Hat’s product‑security advisory. Treat it as a “push‑now” item rather than a “watch‑later” note. [FACT:f6cc391469f2ef05d5bfa785482edb40][FACT:b1bc1b6aaf53c89be761cd985391fb9c]

keyPoints: RHSA‑2026:76134 releases Red Hat Single Sign‑On 7.6.13 for OpenShift with multiple CVE fixes.
All addressed CVEs have CVSS base scores of 7.5 or higher, marking the risk as high.
Upgrade is a pure image bump – no breaking API changes, but token‑handling libraries have been patched.
articles.whyItMatters: AI platforms that rely on OpenShift‑based authentication inherit the SSO image’s vulnerabilities. An unpatched image can let attackers hijack model serving endpoints or steal data, directly threatening cloud‑native AI deployments.
articles.readerAction: Pull the new 7.6.13 image (or update your OpenShift SSO Operator spec) and run your regression suite. Verify token signatures and log any authentication failures before promoting to production.

articles.headline: Dapr Runtime v1.17.15‑rc.1 lands on GitHub
articles.dek: The new release‑candidate bundles bug fixes and updates the default sidecar image for Kubernetes workloads.

body.text: Key Takeaway

On Oct 5 2026 Dapr released version 1.17.15‑rc.1 on GitHub [FACT:dc10aed036e8fd096f218eeb29a60459]. It is marked as a release‑candidate and the assets page lists the usual tarball and Docker images [FACT:004b6bbd0fe28ba006c914caea326119]. The notes call out a set of bug fixes and a minor bump to the default sidecar image tag [FACT:dc10aed036e8fd096f218eeb29a60459].
Why This Matters

For teams running Dapr on Kubernetes the runtime version controls the sidecar that handles pub/sub, state stores, and secret retrieval [FACT:dc10aed036e8fd096f218eeb29a60459]. An RC lets you test those changes before the final 1.17.15 ships, so you can catch regressions early in your CI/CD flow [FACT:dc10aed036e8fd096f218eeb29a60459].
What Happened

The release notes list the fixed issues (e.g., duplicate component registration and a race condition in the health probe) and note that the updated sidecar image is 1.17.15‑rc.1 [FACT:dc10aed036e8fd096f218eeb29a60459]. No new APIs were added, keeping compatibility with existing Dapr applications [FACT:dc10aed036e8fd096f218eeb29a60459].
Builder View

If you pin your deployment to a specific Dapr tag, update the image to 1.17.15‑rc.1 and rollout the pods so the new sidecar is loaded [FACT:dc10aed036e8fd096f218eeb29a60459]. The change also refreshes the built‑in health‑check endpoints, so monitoring dashboards may see a brief status change during the rollout [FACT:dc10aed036e8fd096f218eeb29a60459].
Open Questions

The RC does not publish benchmark data, so performance impact is unknown until you run your own load test [FACT:dc10aed036e8fd096f218eeb29a60459]. The exact timing of the GA release is still pending; keep an eye on the GitHub tag for a final v1.17.15 [FACT:dc10aed036e8fd096f218eeb29a60459].
Ardur Take

One authoritative source confirms the RC release; confidence in the existence of v1.17.15‑rc.1 is high, but downstream effects should be validated in your own cluster before promotion [FACT:dc10aed036e8fd096f218eeb29a60459].
